newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rwanda lets Spain investigate aid worker killings.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda lets Spain investigate aid worker killings.

text.p: The Rwandan government has agreed to allow Spanish police to join a highly-awaited investigation into the January 18 killing of three Spanish aid workers, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
Rwandan military sources say the killers are members of the Hutu Interahamwe militia which led the 1994 slaughter of 800,000 Rwandans.

According to the sources, Hutu gunmen stormed the aid workers' house demanding to see their passports. The men stole money and medicine before shooting the three Spaniards at close range. They also killed three Rwandan soldiers and wounded an American civilian in the attack.
Spanish officials have declined comment on possible motives for the assassinations until after the investigation, which has generated a lot of interest in Spain.
The killings occurred during the return to Rwanda of thousands of refugees at a time when many foreigners from international humanitarian groups were in the country.
